[Model] air purifier review: 30 days in a Delhi November

VERDICT
Buy it if you want to clean one bedroom or a small living room in a 2BHK. You must be able to live with a filter bill of Rs [filter price] every [filter life]. Skip it if you need to clean a hall or an open-plan flat larger than [rated room size]. [Alternative B] does that job better. Price paid: Rs [price paid] at [seller], checked on [date]. Score: [x/10, only if this site scores].

DISCLOSURE
[Confirm one: we bought this unit with our own money / the brand loaned us this unit and has not seen this review]. The buying links in this article go to [Seller 1] and [Seller 2]. They are affiliate links: if you buy through them we earn a commission, and the price you pay does not change.

HOW I TESTED
I used the [Model] for 30 days in November in a 2BHK flat in Dwarka, Delhi. It ran in the bedroom, [hours a day and which fan mode, from the notes]. Morning and night, I took readings with a handheld PM2.5 monitor, first outdoors and then in the bedroom. I also measured noise at each fan speed, noted the filter's price and rated life, and logged how the app behaved day to day. A handheld monitor is not a lab instrument, so read my figures as outside against inside on the same device, not as certified values.

WHAT THE AIR ACTUALLY DID
November is the month Delhi's air is usually at its worst, so it is the right month to test a purifier and a hard one to pass. Before judging the machine I needed a baseline. Outdoors, the monitor read [outdoor morning average] µg/m³ in the morning and [outdoor night average] at night, averaged over [N] days.

In the bedroom with the purifier running, it read [bedroom morning average] in the morning and [bedroom night average] at night. That is [x%] lower than outdoors in the morning and [y%] lower at night. For scale, India's 24-hour standard for PM2.5 is 60 µg/m³ and the WHO guideline is 15. The bedroom [did / did not] get under the Indian figure on [N] of 30 nights, and [did / did not] ever reach the WHO one.

What that means for you: my bedroom is [room size] and the maker rates this machine for [rated area]. A rated area is a ceiling, not a promise. If your room is bigger than mine, expect a smaller drop than I got, and expect the fan to run at a higher, louder speed to get it.

NOISE AT EACH FAN SPEED
I expected the lowest speed to be quiet enough to sleep beside, because a purifier that gets switched off at night does nothing during the hours when you breathe the most. I measured at [distance] from the machine with [instrument].

- Lowest speed: [dB]
- Medium speed: [dB]
- Highest speed: [dB]

[One sentence on which speed I slept on, and whether the lowest speed was enough to keep the bedroom reading down.] The highest speed was [describe: e.g. fine for the hall during the day / too loud to talk over]. If you are a light sleeper, the lowest-speed figure is the one to compare across models.

FILTER PRICE AND LIFE
Running cost decides whether you will keep using a purifier in month seven. The replacement HEPA filter costs Rs [filter price] and the maker rates it for [rated life]. After 30 days in a Delhi November the filter indicator showed [x]% used. If that pace held, the filter would last about [N] months here, not the rated [rated life].

Yearly cost to run: filter [Rs filter price x filters per year] plus electricity [watts at the speed I used x hours x Rs per unit] = about Rs [total] a year. Add that to the Rs [price paid] sticker price before you compare it with a cheaper machine that has a dearer filter.

THE APP
I expected the app to be an extra, and it was [an extra / something I used daily]. What worked: [e.g. schedules, live reading, filter reminder, from the notes]. What did not: [e.g. dropped connection, delayed reading, from the notes]. The machine [can / cannot] be run properly without it; the physical buttons [cover / do not cover] the basics.

PROS
- [Bedroom PM2.5 reading against outdoor, in numbers]
- [Noise at the lowest speed, in dB]
- [Filter price and rated life, if it is good]

CONS
- [Noise at the highest speed, in dB]
- Filter replacement of Rs [price] every [months seen here] adds about Rs [per month] a month
- [App problem I saw, with the day it happened]

WHAT I WOULD CHECK ON ANY PURIFIER AT THIS PRICE
Three questions did most of the work in this test, and they apply to the next machine you look at.
First, does the rated area match your biggest room, with some margin? A machine rated for your exact room size will have to run on a high speed, and a high speed is the loud one.
Second, how loud is the lowest speed, in dB, at a stated distance? Brands usually quote the best figure, so compare the number you measured or a reviewer measured, not the number on the box.
Third, what does the filter cost per year? The sticker price is paid once. The filter is paid again every time it runs out, and in a Delhi November that comes sooner than the label says.

ALTERNATIVES
[Alternative B], Rs [price], rated for [larger area]: the better pick for a hall or any room bigger than [rated room size] in this review. It costs more upfront, and its filter costs Rs [filter price].
[Alternative C], Rs [price]: pick it if you only need a quiet bedroom machine and want to spend less now, and check its filter price before you pay.

WHO SHOULD BUY, WHO SHOULD SKIP
Buy it for a bedroom or small living room up to [rated room size], if you are happy to run it every night and pay for a filter about every [N] months.
Skip it if your main room is a large hall, if you want a machine you can leave on the highest speed all day, or if you will not replace the filter on time. An unchanged filter is a fan that moves dirty air.

After 30 days in Dwarka, my call is [buy / skip] for a room up to [rated room size], and [Alternative B] for anything bigger. Price checked on [date]: [Seller 1 link] Rs [price], [Seller 2 link] Rs [price]. Prices change often, so check the date.

PART-LOAD ROUTE PAGE TEMPLATE: "{{origin}} to {{destination}} part load transport"

1. DATA MODEL AND PUBLISH RULES

Row fields (all required unless marked):
- origin, destination (city names; also origin_slug, destination_slug)
- distance_km (number)
- transit_days (number or range)
- price_min, price_max (Rs per tonne) and data_as_of (month and year, added so every price is dated)
- top_goods (list of 2 or more goods)
- trucks_last_quarter (number)
- interstate (yes or no)
- top_goods_3 (optional)

Publish rules:
1. Publish a page only if every required field is present and valid. A missing price or transit time means no page.
2. trucks_last_quarter of 6 or more: index. 1 to 5: publish with noindex. 0: no page; list the route as a row in the origin hub table only. [Client to set the cut-off.]
3. data_as_of older than two quarters: noindex until the price is refreshed.
4. Two neighbouring pages must differ by more than swapped names: the data table, top_goods and one conditional block must all differ. If they do not, merge or noindex the weaker page.
5. Start with the 20 routes that have the highest trucks_last_quarter. Expand only after they earn impressions and quote requests.
6. Before launch, read the 10 oddest rows (longest names, longest distance, smallest truck count) as rendered pages.

2. TITLE, H1 AND META PATTERNS

Title, use the longest version that fits 60 characters:
a. {{origin}} to {{destination}} Part Load Transport | Rs {{price_min}}-{{price_max}}/tonne | [Brand]
b. {{origin}} to {{destination}} Part Load Transport | [Brand]
c. {{origin}} to {{destination}} Part Load Transport
d. {{origin}} to {{destination}} Part Load
H1: Part load transport from {{origin}} to {{destination}}
Meta: {{distance_km}} km, {{transit_days}} days, Rs {{price_min}} to Rs {{price_max}} per tonne. Part load from {{origin}} to {{destination}}: get a quote for your goods.

3. ANSWER-FIRST INTRO

Part load from {{origin}} to {{destination}} covers {{distance_km}} km and usually takes {{transit_days}} days. Our price band on this route is Rs {{price_min}} to Rs {{price_max}} per tonne, as of {{data_as_of}}, depending on weight and goods. We ran {{trucks_last_quarter}} trucks on it last quarter, mostly carrying {{top_goods}}.

4. DATA BLOCK (this row only)

Distance | {{distance_km}} km
Typical transit | {{transit_days}} days
Price band | Rs {{price_min}} to Rs {{price_max}} per tonne (as of {{data_as_of}})
Goods moved most | {{top_goods}}
Trucks run last quarter | {{trucks_last_quarter}}
Route type | {{interstate_label}}

5. CONDITIONAL BLOCKS

Block A, interstate = yes:
{{origin}} and {{destination}} are in different states, so this is an interstate move. Keep a GST invoice with the goods. For a consignment worth more than Rs 50,000, an e-way bill must be generated before the truck leaves. Tell us the goods value when you book and we will confirm what the load needs. [Client's compliance team to confirm.]
Block A, interstate = no:
{{origin}} and {{destination}} are in the same state, so this is a within-state move. A GST invoice and the lorry receipt travel with the goods. E-way bill rules for movement inside a state vary by state, so send us the goods value and we will tell you if one is needed. [Compliance team to confirm.]

Block B, distance_km is 1,000 or more:
At {{distance_km}} km this is a long-haul route. Part-load goods share the truck with other consignments, so a long route is planned around the truck filling up. Book early and plan for the full {{transit_days}} days.
Block B, distance_km is under 1,000:
At {{distance_km}} km this is a short or medium haul, and most loads reach {{destination}} in {{transit_days}} days. That makes part load a practical choice for regular stock moves when a full truck is more than you need.

6. STEPS FOR THIS ROUTE

1. Send the goods, weight in tonnes and pickup address in {{origin}}.
2. We confirm the rate inside the Rs {{price_min}} to Rs {{price_max}} per tonne band and the pickup date.
3. Keep the GST invoice ready. If interstate = yes, generate the e-way bill too.
4. The truck covers {{distance_km}} km to {{destination}}.
5. Delivery in about {{transit_days}} days; the receiver signs the lorry receipt.

7. FAQS FROM THE ROW

How much does part load from {{origin}} to {{destination}} cost?
Rs {{price_min}} to Rs {{price_max}} per tonne, as of {{data_as_of}}. The rate depends on weight and on what you ship.
How long does it take?
About {{transit_days}} days for {{distance_km}} km.
What goods go on this route?
Mostly {{top_goods}}. We ran {{trucks_last_quarter}} trucks here last quarter.
Do I need an e-way bill?
Interstate = yes: Yes, for goods worth more than Rs 50,000, because this route crosses a state border. Interstate = no: It depends on the state's rule; send us the goods value and we will tell you.

8. INTERNAL LINKS

- Hub: Part load transport across India, /part-load/
- Origin hub: All part-load routes from {{origin}}, /part-load/{{origin_slug}}/
- Reverse route, only if it passes the publish rules: {{destination}} to {{origin}} part load, /part-load/{{destination_slug}}-to-{{origin_slug}}/
- Three nearby routes from {{origin}} by distance, anchor "{{origin}} to {{nearby_destination}} part load"
- How part-load pricing works, /guides/part-load-pricing/
- Get a quote, /quote/

9. CTA

The PDF link is a visible [placeholder] and the affiliation is stated in the last line. 380 words.)
samples.text:
I cleared SSC CGL in 2019 while working full-time at a bank branch, and I now mentor about 40 aspirants a year in Lucknow.

Short answer: split the six months into three phases, 10 weeks of basics, 10 weeks of topic-wise practice and 6 weeks of mocks, and protect a fixed slot every day. I studied 2.5 hours on weekdays and 6 hours on Sundays. That is 18.5 hours a week, and it is enough if you do not skip.

Here is how I spent those hours.

Weeks 1 to 10: basics
- Mon, Wed, Fri: 1.5 hours Maths, 1 hour Reasoning.
- Tue, Thu: 1 hour English, 1 hour General Awareness, 30 minutes revising the previous day's notes.
- Sunday: 3 hours on the chapter you got most wrong that week, 3 hours of untimed practice.
- Rule: one book per subject. Finish it before you buy another.

Weeks 11 to 20: practice
- Weekdays stay the same, but every session is previous-year questions by topic, not new theory.
- Sunday: one timed sectional test, then 3 hours on every question you got wrong or guessed.
- Keep an error notebook. Write the question, your mistake and the right method in one line each.

Weeks 21 to 26: mocks
- Sunday: one full Tier 1 mock under exam timing, then 4 hours of analysis.
- Weekdays: fix only what the last mock showed. Nothing new.
- In the last week, revise your error notebook and do no new topics.

Two things that mattered more than hours. First, revision: with a job it is easy to forget on Thursday what you studied on Monday, so build the 30 minutes of notes into Tuesday and Thursday. Second, Sunday analysis: the mock teaches you nothing until you study why you lost marks. Seedhi baat: analysis hi asli game hai.

When this changes: if you have never done Maths since school, give basics 14 weeks and cut practice to 6. If your job has rotating shifts, fix the 2.5 hours by the clock, not by the day. Check the latest SSC notification for the current exam pattern before you copy my section timings.

I have put the same timetable and the error-notebook format in a free study-plan PDF: [link]. I wrote it and I run the mentoring in Lucknow, so I am affiliated with it.

आज मन में ऊर्जा रहेगी। दफ़्तर में कोई अटकी फ़ाइल या मंज़ूरी आगे बढ़ सकती है। ख़र्च का हिसाब लिखकर चलें, इससे हाथ तंग नहीं होगा। भाई-बहन से फ़ोन पर हालचाल लें। पानी ज़्यादा पिएँ और देर रात तक न जागें। उपाय: सुबह पाँच मिनट शांत बैठकर दिन की योजना बनाएँ।

भावनाएँ आज थोड़ी गहरी रहेंगी, इसलिए सुबह कुछ समय अपने लिए रखें। कामकाज में टीम के साथ तालमेल बनाने से बात बनेगी। धन के मामले में बचत की सोच अच्छी रहेगी। घर की किसी बुज़ुर्ग महिला से बात करना सुकून देगा। पेट हल्का रखें, तला-भुना कम खाएँ। उपाय: शाम को तुलसी के पास दीया जलाएँ।

आज आपकी बात का वज़न रहेगा, पर सुनना भी उतना ही ज़रूरी है। बैठक में पहले दूसरों की राय सुनें, फिर अपनी बात रखें। पुराने लेन-देन का हिसाब मिलाने के लिए अच्छा दिन है। बच्चों के साथ थोड़ा समय बिताएँ। पीठ सीधी रखकर बैठें और बीच-बीच में टहलें। उपाय: सुबह उगते सूरज को जल अर्पित करें।

आज छोटी बातों पर ध्यान जाएगा, और यही आपकी ताक़त बनेगी। रिपोर्ट, बिल या दस्तावेज़ में कोई ग़लती पकड़ में आ सकती है, एक बार जाँच लें। ख़र्च बजट के भीतर रहे तो मन हल्का रहेगा। परिवार में किसी की बात बिना टोके सुनें। खाने का समय नियमित रखें। उपाय: दिन शुरू करने से पहले काम की सूची बनाएँ।

तुला
आज संतुलन बनाना ही सबसे बड़ा काम होगा। दो लोगों के बीच किसी असहमति में आप समझदारी से बीच का रास्ता निकाल सकते हैं। पैसे को लेकर बड़ा फ़ैसला आज टालना बेहतर है। जीवनसाथी के साथ शाम की चाय पर बात करें। कमर और गर्दन को खींचकर आराम दें। उपाय: शाम को पाँच मिनट गहरी साँस लें।

वृश्चिक
आज ध्यान गहरे काम पर टिकेगा। जो काम कई दिन से अधूरा है, उसे आज निपटाने की कोशिश करें। ख़र्च और लेन-देन का हिसाब साफ़ रखें, धन का प्रवाह सामान्य रहेगा। परिवार में कोई पुरानी बात न उठाएँ। नींद पूरी लें और ज़्यादा चाय-कॉफ़ी से बचें। उपाय: घर के किसी एक कोने की सफ़ाई करें।

धनु
आज यात्रा या किसी नई जगह का ज़िक्र उत्साह देगा। अगर काम के सिलसिले में कहीं जाना है, तो जल्दी निकलें और रास्ते का समय देख लें। धन के मामले में आज अनुमान पर नहीं, हिसाब पर चलें। भाई-बहन या मित्र के साथ हँसी-मज़ाक का मौक़ा मिलेगा। घुटनों और पैरों को आराम दें। उपाय: किसी बुज़ुर्ग के साथ कुछ देर बैठें।

मकर
आज मेहनत का फल धीरे-धीरे दिखेगा। अधिकारी या बड़ों से बातचीत में आपकी ज़िम्मेदारी की तारीफ़ हो सकती है। धन के मामले में नियमित बचत की आदत मज़बूत करने का दिन है। परिवार को आज थोड़ा ज़्यादा समय दें। जोड़ों को अकड़ने न दें, हल्का व्यायाम करें। उपाय: काम शुरू करने से पहले दो मिनट आँखें बंद कर धन्यवाद कहें।

कुंभ
नए विचार आज आपके पास आएँगे, उन्हें लिख लें। किसी साथी के साथ मिलकर किया काम अच्छा नतीजा दे सकता है। पैसे के मामले में आज ख़र्च और ज़रूरत का फ़र्क़ समझना ठीक रहेगा। दोस्तों से मुलाक़ात का कार्यक्रम बन सकता है। टखनों और पिंडलियों को आराम दें, बैठते समय पैर ऊँचे रखें। उपाय: एक पुराने मित्र को फ़ोन करें।

मीन
आज मन में दया और कल्पना दोनों रहेंगी। रचनात्मक या सेवा से जुड़े कामों में अच्छा समय है। धन के मामले में आज बहाव के साथ नहीं, योजना के साथ चलें। परिवार के किसी सदस्य की ज़रूरत पर ध्यान दें। पैरों को गुनगुने पानी से आराम दें और समय पर सोएँ। उपाय: शाम को पक्षियों के लिए पानी रखें।

samples.text:
# gstcheck

A command-line tool that checks the format and check digit of every GSTIN in a vendor CSV, offline, and writes the invalid rows to a report.

![MIT licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-MIT-blue) ![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue)

## Why

A mistyped GSTIN in a vendor master causes a failed input-tax-credit match weeks later. `gstcheck` catches the typo before you file. It reads your CSV, tests each GSTIN against the 15-character pattern (state code, PAN, entity number, `Z`, check digit) and recomputes the check digit. Nothing leaves your machine.

`gstcheck` does not tell you whether a GSTIN is registered or active. For that, use the search on the GST portal.

## Quick start

You need Python 3.10 or newer.

```bash
pip install gstcheck
```

Save this as `vendors.csv`:

```csv
vendor,gstin,city
Rathore Traders,08ABCDE1234F1Z0,Jaipur
Kaveri Packaging,29PQRSX5678L1ZS,Bengaluru
Om Sai Stores,27AAAPL1234C1ZX,Pune
Lakshmi Agro,27KLMNO4321P1Z,Nagpur
Patel Brothers,27ABCD12345F1ZX,Mumbai
```

Run it:

```bash
gstcheck vendors.csv
```

You should see:

```text
Checked 5 GSTINs: 2 valid, 3 invalid
  line 4  27AAAPL1234C1ZX  bad check digit (expected E)
  line 5  27KLMNO4321P1Z   wrong length (14, expected 15)
  line 6  27ABCD12345F1ZX  bad format
Report: vendors_invalid.csv
```

`vendors_invalid.csv` holds the three bad rows with all your original columns plus a `reason` column.

## Usage

### Use a different column name

By default `gstcheck` reads a column called `gstin`. If yours is named differently:

```bash
gstcheck vendors.csv --column "GST No"
```

### Choose where the report goes

```bash
gstcheck vendors.csv --output reports/bad_gstins.csv
```

### Fail a script or CI job when any GSTIN is invalid

```bash
gstcheck vendors.csv --fail-on-invalid
```

The command exits with code 1 if it finds an invalid row, and 0 if every row passes.

## Flags

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--column NAME` | `gstin` | Header of the column that holds the GSTINs |
| `--output PATH` | `<input>_invalid.csv` | Where to write the report of invalid rows |
| `--fail-on-invalid` | off | Exit with code 1 if any row is invalid |
| `--encoding NAME` | `utf-8` | Encoding of the input file, for example `cp1252` for older Excel exports |
| `--help` | | Show all flags |

Blank GSTIN cells are skipped and counted, not reported as invalid.

## Help

Questions and bug reports go to the [issue tracker](https://github.com/[user]/gstcheck/issues). A useful report has your Python version, your operating system, the exact command, and the row that gave the wrong result. Please do not paste real vendor names; the GSTIN row alone is enough.

## Contributing

```bash
git clone https://github.com/[user]/gstcheck
cd gstcheck
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest
```

Add a test in `tests/` for every change. Open an issue first if you plan a large change.

## Licence

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Maintained by [maintainer name], Bengaluru.

Bihari litti chokha in a home oven (no tandoor, no coal)

Jump to recipe. The trick is a firm, ghee-rich dough and a hot oven turned down once the vegetables are out.

Litti chokha is a Bihari classic. A wheat dough ball is stuffed with spiced sattu, baked until it cracks, and served with a smoky mash of baingan, aloo and tamatar. Traditionally it is baked over coal or cow-dung embers. Most of us living in Delhi, Pune or Bengaluru have an oven, a tray and an impatient family instead. This version gives you the same cracked, golden shell and the same smoky chokha, using oven heat alone. Read the method once before you start: the dough rests while the vegetables roast, and the oven temperature changes halfway.

AT A GLANCE
Prep: 35 minutes, plus 20 minutes for the dough to rest
Cook: 35 minutes for the littis (the chokha vegetables roast while the dough rests)
Total: about 1 hour 30 minutes
Makes: 12 littis and chokha for 4 people (3 littis each)
Difficulty: medium
Equipment: oven, baking tray lined with baking paper

INGREDIENTS

For the dough
- 360 g atta (whole wheat flour), about 3 cups
- 4 tablespoons ghee (about 50 g), plus 4 tablespoons melted ghee for finishing
- 3/4 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon ajwain (carom seeds)
- About 180 ml water

For the sattu filling
- 120 g sattu (roasted gram flour), about 1 cup
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 4 garlic cloves, finely chopped
- 1 inch ginger, grated
- 2 green chillies, finely chopped
- 2 tablespoons hara dhaniya (coriander leaves), chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon ajwain
- 1/2 teaspoon kalonji (nigella seeds)
- 2 tablespoons raw sarson ka tel (mustard oil)
- 1 tablespoon nimbu (lemon) juice
- 1/2 teaspoon salt, adjust to taste
- 2 tablespoons water

For the chokha
- 2 medium round baingan (brinjal), about 400 g
- 2 medium aloo (potatoes), about 250 g
- 2 medium tamatar (tomatoes), about 200 g
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 garlic cloves, finely chopped
- 1 green chilli, finely chopped
- 2 tablespoons hara dhaniya, chopped
- 1 tablespoon raw mustard oil
- Salt to taste

METHOD
1. Make the dough. Rub 4 tablespoons ghee, the salt and the ajwain into the atta for 2 minutes, until the flour holds its shape when you squeeze a handful in your fist.
2. Add the water a little at a time and knead for 5 minutes to a firm, smooth dough, stiffer than roti dough. Cover and rest it for 20 minutes.
3. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 220 degrees C (fan 210). Boil the potatoes for 15 to 20 minutes, until a knife slides in without resistance.
4. Put the baingan on a tray and roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until the skin is blackened and the flesh collapses when pressed. Add the tomatoes for the last 10 to 12 minutes, until their skins split.
5. Mix the filling. Combine all the filling ingredients with 2 tablespoons water. It should look like damp sand and hold together when you press a spoonful in your palm. Taste and add salt if needed.
6. Lower the oven to 200 degrees C (fan 190). Divide the dough into 12 balls of about 50 g each.
7. Flatten a ball into a small cup and put in 1 heaped tablespoon of filling (about 18 g). Pinch the edges closed, then roll it between your palms into a smooth ball. Seal firmly. Repeat with all 12.
8. Place the littis seam side down on the lined tray, 2 cm apart. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, turning them every 10 minutes, until deep golden-brown with fine cracks, firm to the touch, and hollow when tapped.
9. While they bake, make the chokha. Peel the baingan, potatoes and tomatoes. Drain the baingan in a sieve for 5 minutes. Mash everything roughly with the onion, garlic, chilli, coriander, mustard oil and salt. Keep it chunky.
10. Dunk each hot litti in melted ghee, using about 1 tablespoon each, or brush it on well. Rest 5 minutes in a covered box, then serve with chokha.

AIR-FRYER VARIATION
Shape the littis the same way. Air-fry 4 to 6 at a time, not touching, at 180 degrees C for 18 to 20 minutes, turning once after 10 minutes, until deep golden and firm. Roast the baingan and tomatoes in the oven, or char them directly over a gas flame.

TIPS, SUBSTITUTIONS AND FIXES
- Dough cracks while shaping: it is too dry. Wet your hands and knead for a minute.
- Filling leaks out in the oven: you overfilled or did not seal. Use 1 heaped tablespoon only, and pinch the seam shut.
- Littis turn out hard as stone: the dough had too little ghee or the oven was too hot. Rub in the full 4 tablespoons, and if the outside browns before 25 minutes, drop the oven to 180 degrees C.
- No mustard oil: use any cooking oil, but the taste will be milder.
- No sattu: dry-roast besan on low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until nutty, and cool it before using.

STORAGE AND SERVING
Keep the littis in a closed box for 2 days at room temperature, or 4 days in the fridge. Reheat at 180 degrees C for 8 to 10 minutes. Eat the chokha the same day, or refrigerate it for up to 24 hours. Serve with melted ghee, green chutney, sliced onion and lemon wedges.

FAQ
Can I make the littis ahead? Yes. Bake them completely, store them as above and reheat. Add the ghee after reheating.
Is the sattu raw? No. Sattu is roasted gram flour. Packets marked sattu are ready to use, and raw besan is not a substitute unless you roast it first.
Can I skip the ghee dunk? You can, but the ghee dunk is what makes littis soft and rich, so do not skip it for guests.

(Writer note: DRAFT FOR THE PROFESSOR TO EDIT, SIGN AND SUBMIT HIMSELF. The brief supplies the courses, the 2024 Heat Transfer rank (3rd of 68), the project topic, the rig rebuild and the co-written paper; it supplies no names, dates beyond 2024, rig details, paper details or observations of how she works. All names, the letterhead, the paper's title and conference, the rig specifics and one optional growth sentence are visible [placeholders]; the observation in paragraph 2 and the overall 'strongly' are the professor's to confirm or replace. [College letterhead: name, address, Pune]

[Date]

To the Admissions Committee
[Programme, university]

Dear Members of the Committee,

I am a professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at [College name], Pune, and I am writing to recommend [Student name] for your MS programme. I have known her since 2024, when I taught her Heat Transfer. I later taught her Thermal Systems Design and guided her final-year project. I recommend her strongly, and I would like to give you evidence rather than adjectives.

In 2024 she ranked 3rd among the 68 students in my Heat Transfer course. The rank matters less to me than what came after it: she is the student who kept coming back to the same problem until she could explain why the answer was what it was. [Professor to confirm or replace this observation with a real one.]

Her final-year project, which I guided, was on battery thermal management for electric two-wheelers. Heat is a central design constraint for a battery pack on a two-wheeler running in Indian summers, so the question is a practical one, not a classroom exercise. [One sentence from the professor on her approach, for example the cooling method she compared and what she found.]

Her project needed measurements, so she rebuilt the lab's test rig. [Professor to describe what was wrong with the old rig and whether she took the work on herself or was asked]. [Time it took her, what she changed, and what the rig now measures]. This is the episode I would ask the committee to weigh most. Rebuilding a test rig is unglamorous work that no course requires, and it is the work that decides whether a research result can be trusted. [If true: the rig is now used by other students or projects.]

She then co-wrote a conference paper from the project: [paper title, conference and co-authors, to confirm]. Many strong students in our programme can solve a problem set. Fewer can carry a result from a rig on a bench to a written paper that other engineers can check, and she has done both.

[Optional, and only if true: one honest area she is still developing, with the evidence that she is improving.]

For a programme that values research ability and initiative, I think [Student name] is a candidate who will contribute from her first semester. I recommend her for MS programmes in mechanical engineering, particularly programmes in Germany and the United States that work on thermal systems and energy storage. I expect her to hold her own in either country. Please write to me at the address below if the committee has any questions.

Yours sincerely,

[Signature]
[Professor name]
[Designation], Department of Mechanical Engineering
[College name], Pune
[Official email] | [Phone]
